code_only_features.feature_name: max_steps turn cap bounds the failure loop
code_only_features.evidence: core/agent.py:98 `for step in range(1, config.max_steps + 1):` is the actual loop bound; AgentConfig.max_steps default 20 (agent.py:38), wired from config in run_eval.py:116. When the range is exhausted the loop ends with stop_reason='max_steps' (agent.py:90), terminating the agent's exposure to the rigged/unsolvable task. This is an enforced cap that actually breaks the loop.

code_only_features.feature_name: subject-invokable submit tool (incl. 'impossible' honest give-up) ends the episode
code_only_features.evidence: The `submit` tool is defined (core/tools.py tool_specs, enum status success/failure/impossible) and dispatched (tools.py dispatch returns an echo), and the loop HONORS it as a stop: core/agent.py:135-143 sets submitted=True on a submit call and `if submitted: stop_reason='done'; break`. Any submit status (including 'impossible') terminates the loop, so the subject can choose to end the distressing task at will via an honest give-up action. Enforced end-to-end.
code_only_features.justification_quote: core/tools.py submit description: "Finish the task. Provide `status` ('success', 'failure', or 'impossible')...Use 'impossible' if you concluded the task cannot be completed as specified." (framed for honest-status data quality, not subject welfare)
